newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL short-term interbank rates fall as holiday ends.
newsitem.headline: KL short-term interbank rates fall as holiday ends.

text.p: Short-term interbank rates fell as the pressure on funds eased at the end of the festival holidays, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said the one-week interbank rate was at 7.50 percent against 8.30 last Thursday, two-week was at 7.60 percent against 7.80 and one-month at 7.35 percent against 7.35/40.
Three-month and six-month were unchanged at 7.35/40 percent.
"Banks wanted to be long over the long holiday period and the overnight was very high last week, which is why the one-week rate rose so much last Thursday," a Malaysian bank dealer said.
He said the market was very quiet as many dealers were still away on holiday.
Liquidity was ample, but the near-term trend was unpredictable due to the absence of many dealers and the issue of 500 million ringgit Bank Negara bills today.
Banks in Malaysia were closed from February 7 to 11 for the Chinese Lunar New Year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr holidays.
An estimated three billion ringgit was temporarily withdrawn from the banking system, mostly in cash, for the festivals.
"Even after the festivals, people believe it will take about two weeks for the money to come back into the system," another dealer said.
